title: Living Hope and a Holy Life
summary_text: Peter addresses God's chosen exiles, sanctified by the Spirit according to the Father's foreknowledge. He praises God's mercy for living hope through Jesus Christ's resurrection and an unfading inheritance, while trials test faith on the way to salvation. Prophets searched into the coming grace and Christ's sufferings and glory, now announced in the gospel. Peter calls for hope in that grace and holy living, since Christ's blood redeemed believers from their empty former lives. Having been born again through God's enduring word, they are to love one another deeply.
key_points: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, greets exiles chosen according to God's foreknowledge and sanctified by the Spirit.
Christ's resurrection brings living hope, and trials prove faith as believers await the full revealing of salvation.
The Spirit guided prophets to announce Christ's sufferings and coming glories, serving those now hearing the gospel.
Believers must live in holiness and reverent fear, having been redeemed by Christ's precious blood rather than money.
Obedience to the truth calls for sincere love, and God's enduring word has given believers new birth.

title: God's People Follow the Suffering Christ
summary_text: Peter urges believers to reject malice and deceit and grow in salvation like infants seeking milk. Coming to Christ, God's chosen living stone, they become a holy priesthood offering spiritual sacrifices, a people who have received mercy and proclaim God's greatness. They are to resist the desires of the flesh, live honorably among the Gentiles, and submit to governing authorities as God's servants. Servants must also respect harsh masters and endure unjust suffering for doing right. Christ provides the example: He did not retaliate, but bore their sins so they could leave sin and live in righteousness.
key_points: Believers must abandon deceit and malice and seek nourishment that brings growth in salvation.
Christ is God's precious cornerstone, while those who disobey stumble; believers form a holy priesthood and God's chosen people.
Honorable conduct among Gentiles and submission to rulers show freedom used in God's service rather than for evil.
Servants are told to respect even unreasonable masters; patiently suffering for doing right is commendable before God.
Christ suffered without retaliation, bore sins, and brought wandering believers back to their souls' Shepherd.

title: Honor Others and Suffer for Doing Good
summary_text: Peter tells wives to submit to their husbands with pure conduct and inner gentleness, and husbands to honor their wives as fellow heirs of life. He calls all believers to seek peace, bless those who insult them, and explain their hope gently even when suffering unjustly. Christ, the righteous One, suffered for the unrighteous to bring them to God, and preached to imprisoned spirits who disobeyed in Noah's days. Peter connects the eight people saved through water with baptism, which saves through Jesus Christ's resurrection as a pledge of a clear conscience toward God. Christ now rules above angels and heavenly powers.
key_points: Wives' reverent conduct may win unbelieving husbands, while husbands must honor their wives so their prayers are not hindered.
Peter calls for unity, compassion, blessing instead of retaliation, and pursuit of peace.
Believers must sanctify Christ as Lord in their hearts and explain their hope with gentleness while keeping clear consciences.
Christ suffered for sins, was made alive in the Spirit, and preached to imprisoned spirits who disobeyed in Noah's days.
Peter describes baptism as a pledge of a clear conscience, saving through the resurrection of Christ, who rules over heavenly powers.

title: Serve Others and Endure as Christians
summary_text: Christ's suffering gives believers reason to leave sin behind and live for God's will instead of their former excesses and idolatry. People who abuse them for changing will answer to God, who judges both living and dead. With the end near, Peter calls for prayer, deep love, hospitality, and service that uses God's varied grace to glorify Him through Jesus Christ. Suffering for Christ is cause for joy and blessing, while suffering for wrongdoing is not. Since judgment begins with God's household, those suffering according to His will must trust their faithful Creator and keep doing good.
key_points: Believers must leave their former drunkenness, sexual excess, and idolatry, even when others abuse them for refusing to join.
The gospel reached people now dead so they might live according to God in the spirit despite being judged as men in the flesh.
Peter urges clear minds for prayer, deep love, generous hospitality, and gifts used in service through God's strength.
Those insulted for Christ are blessed by God's Spirit and can rejoice in sharing His sufferings before His glory appears.
Judgment begins with God's household; Peter asks what awaits the ungodly if even the righteous are saved with difficulty.

title: Shepherd Willingly and Stand Firm in Grace
summary_text: Peter appeals to fellow elders to care for God's flock willingly and eagerly, leading by example instead of greed or domination. The Chief Shepherd will reward them with unfading glory when He appears. Younger men must submit to elders, and everyone must show humility, entrust anxieties to God, and resist the devil firmly in faith. Peter assures suffering believers that God, who called them to eternal glory in Christ, will restore and strengthen them. He closes by urging them to stand in God's true grace and sends greetings through Silvanus, from Babylon, and from Mark.
key_points: Elders must shepherd willingly, without greed or domination, as examples awaiting the Chief Shepherd's unfading reward.
Younger men must submit to elders, and all must humble themselves before God, who cares for their anxieties.
Believers must stay alert and resist the devil in faith, knowing fellow believers also suffer throughout the world.
